chunks: Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

The omission (doubt) is only what is between the third and the fourth, and in the two and in the four is of that same status. And whoever forgets and does not know whether he prayed three or four, and his doubt is equal, he should stand and complete (the prayer), then sit, so he performs the Tashahhud and offers Salam, and prays two Rak'at and four Sajdahs while he is seated.

So if his imagination was more towards the four, he should perform Tashahhud and Salam, then recite the Opening of the Book, and bow and prostrate, then recite and prostrate two Sajdahs, and perform Tashahhud and Salam. And if his imagination was more towards the two, he should arise and pray two Rak'at, and perform Tashahhud and Salam.

key_terms.سَجَدَاتٌ: Prostrations (specifically the two prostrations for doubt)
key_terms.سَهْوٌ: Omission or forgetfulness leading to doubt in prayer
key_terms.شَكٌّ: Doubt or uncertainty regarding the number of units prayed
key_terms.وَهْمٌ: Imagination or leaning of the mind towards a specific number

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for correcting prayer when one is equally doubtful between praying three or four Rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between minor doubt (between 3rd and 4th Rak'at) and equal doubt (between 2nd and 4th), prescribing specific corrective actions such as sitting for the final prostrations of doubt (sajdat al-shakk). It reflects the Shia emphasis on precision in ritual prayer, where the ruling adapts based on whether the worshipper's inclination leans toward the higher or lower number of Rak'at, ensuring the validity of the prayer through meticulous adherence to the Prophet's practice.
